narratives.title: The AI buildout is a debt-financed capex bubble that breaks when the money runs out
narratives.statement: As held: capex has run past cash flow and is increasingly debt-funded; the chain below the principals (neoclouds, labs, suppliers) defects first — deferrals, cancellations, shelved deals, rental prices — and the bust arrives through credit transmission rather than through anyone's guidance.
narratives.falsifier: The 2027 capex guides of the principals hold or rise through the Q4 prints with IG below 100, no hyperscaler deal pulled and GPU rental prices flat — the chain keeps paying one more year.

quotes.name: Paul Krugman
quotes.position: The announced AI data center buildout, on plans the largest investment boom in U.S. history relative to GDP, will not happen as planned: it now depends on borrowing and lenders are getting wary (rising CDS spreads, notably CoreWeave and Oracle), and intense public opposition is blocking permits. He argues a slowdown would be good, letting the bubble deflate rather than burst.

quotes.name: Ed Zitron
quotes.position: Zitron argues the AI bubble collapses when the money runs out: debt markets are closing to AI infrastructure and venture capital is drying up; OpenAI's raise fell short of target, Anthropic's amended S-1 shows compute costs rising faster than revenue with enormous commitments, and hyperscaler revenue is inflated by lab compute spending.

quotes.name: Ed Zitron
quotes.position: Zitron argues Anthropic's S-1 describes a company that won't exist once it is public: Q2 2026 was profitable only because of discounted SpaceX compute, commitments ramp sharply from mid-2026, and the IPO and lock-up schedule let insiders sell to retail investors as 'exit liquidity' within a broader AI bubble.

quotes.name: Michael Hartnett
quotes.position: "Buy tech bond 'diamonds-in-rough' as AI hyperscalers up equity issuance, cut buybacks": the bond market is now disciplining the AI boom and AI bonds' long underperformance versus AI stocks is ending. Risk-off persists until the global rate-hiking cycle ends, with relief possible in H1 2027 (peace, lower oil, end of hikes); a year-end rally needs MAGS to hold $70 and SMH to hold $520.

quotes.name: Dario Perkins
quotes.position: In his wargame the AI crash scenario is "now overdetermined": US stocks fall 30%, a cyclical downturn is inevitable as capex and construction jobs fall, but the recession is not especially severe because the Fed has room to cut. Investors should stay diversified globally, not bet against tech too early, and add government bonds only once fragility appears.

quotes.position: The reported Microsoft capex cut reflects slipped delivery milestones for third-party capacity, which shifts cash-flow and bridge-financing stress onto developers while energized capacity earns premium rents.

narratives.title: AI's financing is circular — suppliers fund their customers — so the chain's interdependence hides its risk

quotes.name: James Mackintosh
quotes.position: Circular financing in AI, with chip suppliers funding their own customers through equity stakes, backstops and guarantees, reduces diversification because interdependent companies move together. narratives.statement: As held: FX settlement purchases of $500-600bn a year against a flat PBOC balance sheet, missing reinvested interest and entrusted loans to the policy banks add up to a trillion-dollar gap; the pattern looks like backdoor intervention around a crawling peg.
narratives.falsifier: A PBOC disclosure reconciling the gap, or the renminbi floating outside the band without intervention.

quotes.name: Brad Setser
quotes.position: The EU-China auto deal (a quota on Chinese hybrids) is a reasonable first step that stops the immediate import surge but is not a full answer: China's export surge is driven by collapsing domestic demand and massive excess capacity, Europe lacks a broad Section 301-style instrument and conditions on transplant factories, and without a stronger renminbi safeguards and managed trade will keep spreading.
